chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who goes out to his estate and stays for one day, two days, or three days: does he shorten (the prayer) or pray complete? He (peace be upon him) said: He prays the complete prayer, every time he arrives at an estate from his estates.
ai.seo_question: Does a traveler need to shorten their prayer if they stay at an estate for a few days?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that a traveler visiting their own agricultural estate for one to three days is considered a resident (muqim) rather than a traveler, thereby requiring them to pray the complete four-rak'ah prayer upon arrival. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between temporary transit and established presence, emphasizing that ownership or regular use of a property establishes residency status regardless of the short duration. The hadith underscores the practical application of the 'stay of three days' rule in determining prayer length for those with multiple residences.
